subject: Post-call: model fit, benchmark links, and prompt-set request (ACME)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acme.com>, Jenna Li <jenna.li@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model fit, benchmark links, and prompt-set request (ACME)

Thanks again for taking the call today

good conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment:

1) Key asks from ACME
- Collect a representative prompt set (user queries + edge cases) including examples with redaction requirements.
- Confirm success criteria: latency under 350ms p50 for short responses, top-1 relevance >= 92% for QA tasks, and no unacceptable hallucinations on financial records.

2) Redwood recommendations (high-level)
- For ACME's customer-support/QA mix: start with rw-lumi-13b and rw-lumi-70b-compat (quantized) for balance of quality/cost.
- For high-safety/factual tasks, we recommend the 70b-quant variant with our stricter decoding profile.

3) Evals & Benchmarks
- I attached a prompt_collection_template.csv to capture examples and meta (intent, expected output, redaction flags).
- Shared our preliminary eval run: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/EV-12345 (public to ACME invite).

4) Action items
- ACME: upload prompt set + mark edge cases and PHI/PII rows by EOD Thu (Aug 13).
- Redwood: provide a short prompt guide and suggested prompt templates + a redaction checklist by Wed (Aug 12).
- Schedule: 30-min follow-up on Aug 14 to review collected prompts and pick model candidate.

Notes on redaction: please mark any fields that must be redacted at generation time vs stored as hashed IDs. If you're unsure, flag as "possible PII" in the template and include the sensitivity level.

Attachments: prompt_collection_template.csv

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Li <jenna.li@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit, benchmark links, and prompt-set request (ACME)

Thanks Marissa

appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- We'll upload a first-pass prompt set by Thu (Aug 13). Expect ~1200 rows: 60% typical support questions, 25% trick/edge cases, 15% redaction-sensitive items.
- On redaction: our security team prefers that PHI be redacted before sending to any external API. For test purposes we can provide masked examples (e.g., "[REDACTED_NAME]") and a small subset of synthetic unredacted examples in a red-team bucket that we keep locally.

I've attached a small sample workbook (acme_example_prompts.xlsx) in this reply for format reference. Also sharing the Drive link to the full doc here: https://drive.google.com/acme/shared-prompt-collection

Question: when you say "stricter decoding profile" for the 70b-quant variant, can you confirm what we should expect for latency and token-cost delta vs the 13b run? Basic numbers are fine.

Onboarding: can we add a brief Slack channel for real-time triage during the prompt collection window? Jenna will own the uploads.

—Sam
Sam Carter
Senior Product Manager, ACME Corp
sam.carter@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit, benchmark links, and prompt-set request (ACME)

Great, thanks Sam

this is perfect. A few answers to your questions:

- Latency/cost delta (approx): rw-lumi-13b

 p50 ~180-240ms, cost baseline X. rw-lumi-70b-quant (safety profile)

 p50 ~320-380ms, token-cost ~2.7x baseline. Exact numbers depend on sequence length and batch settings; we can run a quick micro-benchmark on your sample prompts once uploaded.

- "Stricter decoding profile" = tighter temperature/top-p settings, stronger repetition penalty, and an extra heuristic to favor shorter, more conservative completions for numerical/financial fields. We can share the exact decoding config in the follow-up doc.

- Redaction guidance: please include both a masked and synthetic-unmasked example when possible. Mark rows with a "sensitivity" column: LOW | MED | HIGH. For HIGH rows we recommend doing offline synthetic examples only and only sending masked live prompts. We'll also share a short checklist for automated redaction rules you can run pre-send (regex patterns + heuristics).

Next steps from Redwood (deliverables by Wed, Aug 12):
- Prompt guide and prompt templates (one-pager).
- Redaction checklist + sample regexes.
- A short eval baseline report showing sample-run outputs for rw-lumi-13b vs rw-lumi-70b-quant for 50 of your prompts (link to be posted to eval console).

I've attached the prompt template again for convenience. I'll ping to schedule the Aug 14 follow-up once Jenna confirms availability.

Best,
Marissa
